entries.name: Gen 3 Box
entries.tagline: Storage as a Ruby and Sapphire style grid you can search, sort and mark.
entries.description: A Ruby/Sapphire-style storage screen over Gen 1's twelve boxes of twenty: a visible 5x4 grid drawn from the per-species battle pics, a cursor that picks a Pokemon up and puts it down, swapping on an occupied slot, and SELECT to cross between the box and the party. Search every box by species, type, or mark with FIND; sort by dex, level, name, or type with UNDO; mark Pokemon with the four Gen 3 symbols; give each box a custom name up to eight glyphs and pick a wallpaper from six patterns; and hear a cry every time a Pokemon lands. BOX HEALS rests everything in storage when you close the screen. GRID BIG doubles the surface to 320x288, showing battle pics at full size and giving each Pokemon its own species palette. OW SPRITES (on by default) draws Wilds of Kanto's overworld sprites in the CLASSIC grid when that mod is installed. It runs on Gold as well as on Red, Blue and Yellow: Gen 2's fourteen boxes, its split Special, its own summary screen and its MAIL rules are all honoured.

entries.name: Gen 3 Dex
entries.tagline: The Pokedex as a grid of pictures, every owned species in its own colours.
entries.description: The Pokedex as a grid of pictures instead of a list of names. Owned species wear their own palette -- twenty-one colours at once where the Game Boy could show four -- seen-but-uncaught are dimmed, and the rest are blanks. SELECT filters to OWNED, MISSING or SEEN ONLY. A offers DATA / CRY / AREA like the vanilla list -- AREA is the engine's own nest map, which blinks every place the species lives. DATA goes to the engine's own species page, so Useful Dex's extra pages still work. Runs on Gold too: fourteen rows of Johto instead of stopping at Mew, the caught half of the dex read where Gold keeps it, DATA/AREA routed to Gold's own dex entry, and GRID BIG now draws its full 320x288 grid there as well, through Gold's own widescreen contract -- without the per-species palette zones, which stay a Super Game Boy trick Gold has no use for.

entries.name: Groovy Palette & Frames
entries.tagline: Thirty more colour schemes and eight text box borders, previewed on the running game.
entries.description: Thirty more entries on the COLORS row -- Amiga Workbench, the C64 boot screen, a Virtual Boy, rainbow, fuchsia, vaporwave -- plus eight new borders for every text box and menu. Press A on OPTION -> COLORS (or, on Gold, OPTION -> COLOR) and the menu lifts off the game: the palette name and nothing else, left and right to walk the list, previewed on the running game. USE ADVANCED rides the engine's own per-tile colorization instead of replacing it -- the pokered-gbc pack on Red/Blue/Yellow, Gold's own GBC palettes on Gold -- so a palette recolours dozens of colours on screen rather than four. The FRAME half works identically on both generations, through the same Font.drawBox both draw their boxes with; the palette half now does too, riding Gold's own GbcPalette.resolve the same way it rides PaletteFX.effectiveColors on Gen 1. The one gap: Gold's title screen and Gold/Silver boot cinema keep their own pre-rendered art (the same boundary its DMG and CLASSIC color modes already live with) and pick up the scheme from the first menu or map onward.

entries.name: Modern Johto
entries.tagline: Gold gets the Gen 4 physical and special split, decided move by move.
entries.description: The Gen 4 physical/special split for Pokemon Gold, decided per move instead of per type -- so Crunch comes off Attack, Shadow Ball off Special Attack, and Gyarados finally throws Hydro Pump off the stat it was never meant to use. Gold already splits Special into two stats, which is what makes the per-move category the real Gen 4 change here rather than the half-measure it is on a game with one Special. Now also an AI toggle: a trainer class that never carries the TYPES bit reads type effectiveness anyway, through a second ai_classes layer that steps aside for any class Gold already made type-aware. Both toggles off by default, because both change the balance. The Gen 2 counterpart of Modern Kanto, which stays where it is: five of that mod's six pieces have nothing to fix on Gold.

entries.name: Modern Kanto
entries.tagline: Six fixes for Gen 1's oldest complaints, from the type chart to the 1 in 256 miss. Still in beta.
entries.description: BETA. Six changes that each answer the same complaint about Gen 1: the Gen 4 physical/special split as per-move data, the four type-chart rows Gen 2 corrected (including the Ghost-does-nothing-to-Psychic bug), a ruleset that fixes five battle rules Gen 1 got wrong by accident (the 1/256 miss, Focus Energy quartering crits, crits ignoring stat stages, the enemy's free PP, Hyper Beam's missing recharge), the player-only badge stat boost as a switch, an AI type pass that multiplies dual types out instead of reading one row, and an Atlas screen for what lives where and what you still need. Every piece is separately switchable; the balance-changing ones are off by default.

entries.name: Pokemon Snag
entries.tagline: Steal a Pokemon out of a trainer battle, then fence it on Kanto's black market.
entries.description: Steal Pokemon from other trainers with the SNAG BALL. It works in trainer battles, so any Pokemon an opponent sends out is one you can take. On Red, beat the TEAM ROCKET recruiter at Nugget Bridge to earn your first, then fence stolen Pokemon to black-market buyers across Kanto. entries.name: Run Mode
entries.tagline: Hold B to run on the overworld.
entries.description: Hold or toggle B to run on the overworld. Open RUN MODE in OPTIONS.

entries.name: Running Shoes
entries.tagline: Hold B to move faster, at a speed you choose, with a trail off your heels.
entries.description: Hold B to walk faster, at a speed you pick: x1.5, x2, x3 or x4. Rides the engine's own movement.speed hook, whose comment names running shoes as the reason it exists. A run can leave a trail off your heels -- smoke, flames or lightning -- reaching about three and a half cells back; it can CUT the tall grass you run across, one clod at a time, the way the CUT move cuts it, so that grass has no Pokemon left in it; and it can carry you through tall grass without ever starting a wild battle. Every one of those has an off switch, the last two ship off, and with all three left alone nothing but the duration of a step changes. Optional boosts for the bicycle and for surfing too. Runs on Pokemon Gold too, and as of 1.6.0 every row works there: RUN SPEED, BOOST BIKE, BOOST SURF, SAFE GRASS, CUT GRASS and RUN FX all cross over. 1.7.0 adds the Dramatic Shape voxel mod's first- and third-person cameras, which replace the grid walk with a continuous one and used to leave every row of this mod silent; the speed, CUT GRASS and SAFE GRASS all work inside them now. RUN FX still cannot: a 2D overlay cannot follow a 3D camera.

entries.tagline: Work the buttons while the ball wobbles to turn a near miss into a catch.
entries.description: The playground legend, made real: working your technique while the ball wobbles can flip a break-free into a catch. Pick your ritual -- mash A+B, hold Down and mash B, hold Up+A, tap A on the beat, hold B and rock the d-pad, or build your own. Vanilla odds are untouched -- it only ever redeems a throw that already gripped and shook.
